findings.text: When a class already has __rich_repr__ defined, the angular parameter passed to @auto(angular=True) is silently ignored because cls.__rich_repr__.angular is only set when auto-generating __rich_repr__. The auto_repr function reads angular from the method attribute, defaulting to False, so angular=True has no effect on classes with existing __rich_repr__.

The auto_rich_repr function assumes all __init__ parameters correspond to instance attributes. If a parameter is not stored as an attribute (e.g., used only for computation), getattr(self, name) will raise AttributeError, causing repr() to fail with a ReprError even though the class is valid.
